newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin taken to hospital with signs of pneumonia.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin taken to hospital with signs of pneumonia.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin was taken to hospital on Wednesday with first signs of pneumonia, raising new fears about his health two months after major heart surgery.

The Kremlin said doctors who examined Yeltsin on Wednesday evening ordered the 65-year-old president back to the Central Clinical Hospital in Moscow where he recuperated after his quintuple bypass on November 5.

The president, who had been looking pale and tired, had already cancelled all appointments since Monday because of what the Kremlin said was a heavy cold. Doctors said the cold was not related to the operation and did not threaten his heart.
"Doctors have stated that the first signs of pneumonia developing have appeared," a Kremlin statement said.
"In connection with this, in order to make a better diagnosis and to conduct appropriate treatment, a decision has been taken to take him to the Central Clinical Hospital for several days."

A Kremlin spokesman confirmed Yeltsin had entered hospital at about nine p.m. (1800 GMT) but gave no details. He did not mention the trigger which controls Russia's nuclear arsenal but it usually accompanies Yeltsin at all times.
Yeltsin, who suffered two heart attacks in 1995 and spent much of last year out of the Kremlin with health problems, had been resting at a country residence outside Moscow because of his illness.

Yeltsin, who played a major role in ending communist rule in 1991 and overseeing economic reforms, has been president since the same year. He fought a tough re-election campaign last year but fell ill just before the decisive round of voting on July 3.
He returned to work in the Kremlin following surgery only on December 23.

Pioneering heart surgeon Michael DeBakey, who advised the Russian doctors who carried out the operation on Yeltsin, said he expected him to make a quick recovery from what he said was probably a case of the flu.
"I expect him to be alright, and I would say that in a matter of three days to a week you're going to see improvement and (he'll) probably leave the hospital," DeBakey said in an interview on CNN.

DeBakey said he had spoken to one of the doctors treating the president. The doctors had found "a spot of pneumonitis" in one of Yeltsin's lungs, he said, but that it had been caught before it could develop into a full-blown case of pneumonia.
Both pneumonia and pneumonitis involve inflammation of the lung.
One of Yeltsin's bitter foes, Alexander Lebed, said the president was too old and sick to govern.

"Our country is headed by a very sick and elderly man. He needs to retire since he can neither govern due to the state of his health nor lead a normal life," Lebed said in remarks broadcast by Moscow radio station Ekho Moskvy.

Yeltsin's long absence from the Kremlin last year fuelled a struggle for position among Kremlin officials that culminated in Lebed's sacking as national security adviser in October. Yeltsin accused him of having presidential ambitions.

Foreign experts, offering initial impressions, told Reuters the pneumonia was probably not related to Yeltsin's heart problems and surgery. They said there was a good chance of recovery if the disease was treated quickly.

The president had been holding regular meetings since his return to the Kremlin, including talks with German Chancellor Helmut Kohl last Saturday, at which the Kremlin leader looked pale and ill at ease.
His last meetings were on Monday, when he discussed relations with NATO with top Russian leaders, and held a separate meeting with Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin.
Under the constitution, Chernomyrdin would stand in for up to three months before a new election if Yeltsin was unable to govern. He stepped in for a day when Yeltsin had his bypass.
The 58-year-old prime minister, a loyal Yeltsin ally, had been due to start a brief leave on Wednesday but it was not clear if he had left Moscow.
Yeltsin's press secretary said on Monday the president had a "heavy cold" and a temperature of 37.5 degrees Celsius (99.5 Fahrenheit) but that it had nothing to do with his heart.
Russian media said several of the president's family, including his younger grandson Gleb and his wife Naina, had fallen victim to a flue epidemic sweeping Moscow over New Year.
Russian Finance Minister Alexander Livshits was also taken to hospital on Wednesday with a high temperature and suspected influenza, Interfax news agency said.
It said Livshits, 50, had been taken, like Yeltsin, to the Central Clinical Hospital. He would have tests on Thursday.
